newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki back on falling trend in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki back on falling trend in thin trade.

text.p: Shares drifted lower on Thursday in listless trade, and brokers expected low activity to persist for some time amid uncertainty about U.S. interest rates. They saw little that could reverse the weak trend.

The HEX index closed 0.82 percent lower at 2,849.16 points, and the so-called yield index, adjusted for shares going ex-dividend, fell 0.78 percent. The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark fell 0.99 percent to 993.55 points.
Volume was a modest 379 million markka with 25 percent in bourse engine Nokia which traded around its 303.50 markka New York closing all day, closing at 304.80, down 4.10.
"It seems lower turnover will continue for a while, after the bumper trade after the turn of the year," one broker said.

Brokers said European markets should break away from the Wall Steet's influence since the old continent has a different economic cycle and rates should stay low, but psychology was in the way. "Not many trade on fundamentals," said one.

Forestries underperformed, but brokers were mixed on whether this was due to an announcement from Swedish SCA that it had delayed a fina paper price hike. UPM-Kymmene fell 2.50 markka to 113.50, and the sub-index fell 1.61 percent.
The overall trend has been falling since the HEX peaked just above 3,000 points on March 11, though this week started with a cautious recovery, brokers said.
"I think this market will be interest rate driven until the U.S. mid-May FOMC meeting, and thus falling," one broker said, adding he did not think a new U.S. rate hike was yet priced in.

There was no major overall focus but one broker reported strong interest in an ongoing IPO from Nordic Aluminium, and fund managers said demand for new issues would stay lively despite current jitters.
